_headline: EUROSTAT'S OWN METADATA PAGE STATES A DOCUMENTED DEPENDENCY BETWEEN TWO NAMED EU STATISTICAL PRODUCTS: 'Both the censuses and the sample surveys are aimed at producing a variety of information on specific CAP targets, as well as providing a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data.' That is the closest thing to a genuine EU-internal statistics-to-statistics edge this branch has found -- every prior EU finding has been about the asymmetry between the supranational and national layers, not a dependency running entirely within the EU statistical system itself.
_open_questions: DOMAIN GAP, same shape as the institutional-budget nodes' fiscal-transfers placeholder. Research.1.md 6's Domain union has no 'agriculture' or 'statistics' value. 'population' is used here as least-wrong -- the Farm Structure Survey is structurally a census/structural-survey instrument (it runs on a 10-year agricultural-census cycle explicitly modelled on population censuses, per its own preamble's reference to the FAO World Programme for the Census of Agriculture), which is a closer analogy than any of national-accounts, labour, or the fiscal/benefits domains. Flagged rather than assumed correct; extend the union at the other end if a better fit is wanted.

CADENCE is a genuine number this time, not a guess, but it changed regime partway through the record. Historically (1989/90 through 2016) reference years averaged roughly one every 2.6 years. Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 fixes the current regime at exactly 2020, 2023, 2026 -- a flat 3-year interval -- with dissemination stated as '2 years after the reference year' (a publication lag, not a frequency). releases_per_year is set to 0.33 to match the current, legally-fixed regime rather than the longer historical average; if a future session weights the full 1966-2026 run instead, the number would come out closer to 0.4.

The FSS -> FADN dependency (see _dropped) is not minted as an edge because FADN itself is not yet a node. FADN's own authoritative site (agridata.ec.europa.eu / agriculture.ec.europa.eu) was unreachable from this environment this session -- denied by the browser tool, cause not established. Everything known about FADN's current public-facing form comes from the legal instruments (Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009, Regulation (EU) 2023/2674) rather than from FADN's own metadata, which is a weaker evidence position than the one this node itself rests on. A future session should retry those two domains before minting FADN.

reports.title: Farm Structure Survey (FSS)
reports.description: Eurostat's recurring survey of the structure of agricultural holdings across the EU, run in one form or another since 1966. Eurostat's own metadata page states: 'The data describe the structure of agricultural holdings providing the general characteristics of farms and farmers and information on their land, livestock and labour force. They also describe production methods, rural development measures and agro-environmental aspects... The aggregated results are disseminated through statistical tables.' Legally re-founded by Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 ('on integrated farm statistics'), which fixed the current data collections at reference years 2020, 2023 and 2026 -- a census in 2020, sample surveys in 2023 and 2026 -- each covering at least 98% of the EU's utilised agricultural area and livestock units. Eurostat's own metadata states the FSS 'provid[es] a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data' -- see _dropped.
reports.cadence_note: Currently fixed at reference years 2020, 2023, 2026 by Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 Article 5 -- a 3-year interval, with results 'disseminated 2 years after the reference year' (Eurostat metadata page, 'Frequency of dissemination'). Historically (1989/1990 through 2016) reference years averaged roughly one every 2.6 years on a 10-year agricultural-census cycle with 2-3 intermediate sample surveys between censuses. See _open_questions.

_dropped.why: THE BEST LEAD THIS SLICE PRODUCED. Eurostat's own 'Farm structure (ef)' metadata page states: 'Both the censuses and the sample surveys are aimed at producing a variety of information on specific CAP targets, as well as providing a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data.' Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 Article 5(3) caps FADN's sample at 'the maximum number of returning holdings shall be 105 000 for the Community' -- a sample that needs a population framework to extrapolate to the whole farming sector, which is what this record says the FSS supplies. Direction, if minted: FADN depends on FSS (methodology_depends_on), because FSS is the structural/weighting framework, not FADN's raw accountancy data. NOT MINTED because FADN itself has no independently-verified title, cadence or URL from its own authoritative site -- agridata.ec.europa.eu and agriculture.ec.europa.eu were both unreachable this session (browser tool denial, cause not established). Everything known about FADN comes from the legal instruments rather than from a FADN-published source, which is a weaker evidence position than Research.1.md 4 asks for before minting. Full quotes in EU/FSDN_FSS_PartA_2026-08-05.md, records FSS-02 and FSDN-01.

_dropped.edge: European Commission annual report on the situation of agriculture and farm incomes -> (no target; the report itself was the candidate node)
_dropped.why: A DOCUMENTED CHANGE, NOT ADJUDICATED. As originally codified in 2009, Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 Article 1(3) required: 'The data obtained pursuant to this Regulation shall, in particular, serve as the basis for the drawing up of reports by the Commission on the situation of agriculture and of agricultural markets as well as on farm incomes in the Community. The reports shall be submitted annually to the European Parliament and the Council, in particular for the annual fixing of prices of agricultural produce.' That is AGENCY ONLY under Research.1.md 6 (no title given for the reports) but otherwise the cleanest annual-report obligation found anywhere in the EU branch. Regulation (EU) 2023/2674 replaced Article 1 in full; the replacement text (read directly, first-hand) contains no equivalent clause -- in its place, a duty to 'make the results of those analyses publicly available in the form of aggregated and anonymised FSDN data', with no stated cadence. Whether the annual-report duty survives elsewhere in the current consolidated text of Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 was not checked; only the amending regulation's own replacement text was read. NOT MINTED on either reading: the 2009 version because it names no title, the 2023 version because it states no cadence. Full quotes in EU/FSDN_FSS_PartA_2026-08-05.md, records FSDN-01 and FSDN-02.

_dropped.edge: eurostat-farm-structure-survey -> ESA 2010 / any other EU statistical framework
_dropped.why: Checked while reading Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 in full: the regulation names Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 (the framework for European statistics generally) as its quality/confidentiality framework, and names the FAO's Global Strategy to Improve Agricultural and Rural Statistics and World Programme for the Census of Agriculture 2020 as the international standards it 'should, where appropriate, follow' -- 'follow the recommendations of' reads as the same 5a-shaped agreement language that ruled out esa-2010 -> sna-2008, not a dependency. No document read this session ties the FSS to ESA 2010 or any other national-accounts framework already in the corpus.
